\chapter{Review --- Six Words That Arrived Last}
\label{ch:repaso-seis-palabras}
\hlchaptermodality{335}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can give la pareja, el bebe, la entrada, el cambio, el calor and la edad from the English, each with its article.}

Complete ES-C335-repaso-seis-palabras: name the noun that is both a doorway and a ticket, name the one that is both an exchange and the coins, and give all six back from the English.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[(review)]{Review --- six words that arrived last}

\label{lesson:ES-C335-repaso-seis-palabras}



\begin{quote}
Two people to begin. Who is \emph{la pareja}? (A couple, or one half of one.) And who is \emph{el bebé}? (A baby.)
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Six nouns, sharing something that has nothing to do with meaning: each one arrived at the end of its run. A word met in the middle of a run gets picked up by everything that comes after it. A word met last has nothing after it, so it was said once and then left alone. These six are here for a second hearing.

\textbf{Two people.} \emph{La pareja} --- a couple, from Latin \emph{par}, equal. \emph{El bebé} --- a baby, and the accent pulls the weight onto the last beat.

\textbf{Two things a stranger holds out to you.} \emph{La entrada} --- the way in, and the ticket that buys the way in. \emph{El cambio} --- the exchange, and the coins pressed back into your hand.

\textbf{Two reports from your own body.} \emph{El calor} --- heat. \emph{La edad} --- age.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
English first, then the Spanish with its article.

Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{the partner} --- \emph{la pareja}
  \item \emph{the baby} --- \emph{el bebé}
  \item \emph{the way in} --- \emph{la entrada}
  \item \emph{the change} --- \emph{el cambio}
  \item \emph{the heat} --- \emph{el calor}
  \item \emph{the age} --- \emph{la edad}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which two of the six name a person? (\emph{La pareja}, \emph{el bebé}.) Which two would a stranger hand you? (\emph{La entrada}, \emph{el cambio}.) Which two report on your own body? (\emph{El calor}, \emph{la edad}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
